title: Adentris vs mdhub: Behavioral Health Documentation Compared
summary: Adentris vs mdhub for behavioral health and SUD: an all-in-one AI scribe and practice OS versus a real-time revenue integrity layer on any EHR, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and denials.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** mdhub and Adentris both bring AI to behavioral health documentation, but they solve different halves of the problem. mdhub is an AI co-pilot and practice operating system for behavioral health clinics, with an ambient scribe, scheduling, intake, and billing in one place. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note, however it was written, in real time before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module built in, running on any EHR. If your problem is documentation time and running the practice, mdhub is built for that. If your problem is denials and audit exposure, that is where Adentris focuses.


Because they emphasize different jobs, the honest comparison is less about which is better and more about which problem you are solving right now. Here is the breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is not a scribe: it does not write the note, it makes sure the note will get paid. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What mdhub does


mdhub is an AI operating system for behavioral health clinics. Its ambient scribe, Emma, drafts clinical documentation from individual therapy to psychiatric evaluations in formats like SOAP, DAP, BIRP, and progress notes within seconds of a session ending, and mdhub also handles scheduling, intake, and billing in its own platform. It is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified. For practices that want an all-in-one AI co-pilot and EHR built for mental health, mdhub is a strong, focused option.

## Where each fits


mdhub is built to run the behavioral health practice: draft the note, schedule, intake, and bill in one platform. Adentris is built for a narrower revenue-integrity job that sits on top of whatever EHR you use: catch the documentation gaps that get behavioral health and SUD claims denied and fix them before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and a paired appeals workflow. Because Adentris connects through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, it can run on mdhub or on any other EHR without a migration. A clinic can use mdhub to generate the note and manage the practice and Adentris to make sure the documentation gets paid.


## Adentris as an mdhub alternative for revenue integrity


If your clinic uses mdhub, or is evaluating it, and the gap you feel is not documentation time but denied claims and audit exposure, that is a different job. Adentris focuses on the payer side: it checks whether the documentation supports the claim, flags the behavioral health and SUD elements that drive denials, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs that with an appeals and denials workflow. Because it runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, it works whether you stay on mdhub or run another system. For clinics that generate notes and manage the practice well but still lose claims, it is a natural complement.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. ## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and mdhub?**


mdhub is an AI co-pilot and practice operating system for behavioral health clinics, with an ambient scribe (Emma), scheduling, intake, and billing in its own platform. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note in real time before the claim is submitted, drafts corrections, and has SUD-specific rules like ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals module built in, running on any EHR. mdhub helps write the note and run the practice; Adentris makes sure the claim gets paid.


**Can Adentris and mdhub be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use mdhub to draft the note and run the practice and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside mdhub.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to mdhub?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than documentation time and practice management, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. mdhub is strong for ambient documentation and all-in-one practice management for behavioral health. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
